exposure: Mind maps assisting midwives in labor pain management
cohort: 100 pregnant women selected for labor, divided into an observation group (n=50) and a control group (n=50).
finding: Mind map assisting midwives in labor pain management significantly enhanced patients' self-efficacy, reduced cesarean delivery rate, reduced pain, obtained an ideal delivery experience, improved nursing satisfaction, and improved the quality of life.
mod_finding: The vaginal delivery rate was higher and the cesarean delivery rate was lower in the observation group compared to the control group.
